---
title: "drosophila"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
set.seed(42)

#Data about mutation rates in drosophila
dros_raw <- read_csv("data/drosophila_counts.csv")

dros_summary <- summarise(dros_raw, 
                          total_nm = sum(Novel_Mutation_Count),
                          max_nm = max(Novel_Mutation_Count),
                          mean_nm = mean(Novel_Mutation_Count),
                          variance_nm = var(Novel_Mutation_Count))

gt(dros_summary)

ggplot(dros_raw,
       aes(
         x = Novel_Mutation_Count
       )) + 
  geom_bar()
```

Want to know whether this data is Poisson distributed - we have a slight discrepancy between mean and var.
One way to do figure out whether it is Poisson is to simulate observations of same sample size (17) from a true Poisson, and look at the magnitude of discrepancies in these simulations, to compare to our discrepancy.

```{r}

sim_mean <- c()
sim_var <- c()
sim_dif <- c()


for (i in 1:1000) {
samplemean = dros_summary |> pull(mean_nm)

simulated_counts <- rpois(
  n = 17,
  lambda = samplemean
)
sim_mean <- c(sim_mean, mean(simulated_counts))
sim_var <- c(sim_var, var(simulated_counts))
sim_dif <- c(sim_dif, abs(mean(simulated_counts) - var(simulated_counts)))
}

df_sim <- tibble(
  mean = sim_mean,
  var = sim_var,
  dif = sim_dif
)


ggplot(
  df_sim,
  aes(
    x = dif
  )
) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density))) + 
  ggtitle("Distribution of differences between mean and var from simulations") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2.01, color="red")
```
